briefs.headline: Gurugram tops residential launches at ₹1.38 lakh cr in 2025; NCR sees 450% post-Covid appreciation
briefs.deck: Only four cities—Gurugram, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Hyderabad—crossed the ₹1 lakh crore mark in residential launch and sales value
briefs.bodyText:
Gurugram emerged as India’s top residential market by launch value in calendar year 2025, recording ₹1.38 lakh crore across 23,809 units, with an average value of over ₹6 crore per unit, according to real estate analytics firm PropEquity.
Only four cities—Gurugram, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Hyderabad—crossed the ₹1 lakh crore mark in residential launch and sales value, the firm said.
Bengaluru recorded ₹1.30 lakh crore across 72,250 units, while Mumbai clocked ₹1.27 lakh crore from 29,627 units and Hyderabad generated ₹1.16 lakh crore from 52,388 units.
“NCR, especially Gurgaon, can no longer be ignored by any top developer as it is not a volume-led real estate story but a value and profit-maximisation-led growth engine, where rising wealth, premiumisation, migration and high employment generation are coming together to redefine India’s next real estate cycle,” said Samir Jasuja, founder and CEO of PropEquity.
“The opportunity is no longer simply about building more—it is about building better, in the right locations and for a more sophisticated homebuyer,” he added.
The overall National Capital Region (NCR) market recorded ₹2.16 lakh crore across 50,167 units, translating into an average value of ₹4 crore per unit, PropEquity said.
Post-Covid, NCR property prices have appreciated 450%, compared with an average of 250% across other cities, the firm said, attributing the sharper rise to a demand-supply mismatch.
“NCR has the highest population among Tier 1 cities (about 3 crore) yet the lowest number of launches at about 50,000 units. This is as compared with Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), which has a population of about 2.5 crore but a total supply of over 1.4 lakh units,” it said.
“This creates a demand–supply mismatch of about 3:1 in favour of NCR compared to the other top cities—the main reason behind NCR’s higher appreciation,” it added.

briefs.headline: AI data-centre boom puts India’s power grid under pressure, drives up upgrade costs
briefs.deck: Electricity officials around India are grappling with the many ways Artificial Intelligence infrastructure is reshaping power transmission dynamics.
briefs.bodyText:
In July, the North Eastern Regional Power Committee (NERPC) convened a special meeting with grid operators and Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. (PGCIL) to address an urgent issue: maintenance contracts for the region’s integrated electricity grid were nearing expiry, necessitating discussions on upgrading the systems.
The financial implications were significant. PGCIL informed the meeting that the estimated cost of upgrading the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition/Energy Management System (SCADA/EMS) at the region’s State Load Despatch Centres had risen from ₹521 crore to about ₹688 crore. The reason: AI-driven demand was making hardware used in supervisory systems more expensive.
Escalating costs are not new to the power sector. As manufacturers phase out older components and specialists capable of maintaining legacy systems become harder to find, replacement and maintenance costs can rise sharply. However, the rapid expansion of data-centre projects is adding a new layer of pressure on power generation and transmission infrastructure.
Ramping concerns
NERPC is not the only regional body grappling with the implications of AI-driven electricity demand.
At a meeting of the Eastern Regional Power Committee’s Technical Coordination Committee last December, an Odisha representative flagged the potential “ramping impact” on States when industries such as data centres undertake “bulk collective purchase” of electricity.
Such fluctuations can strain slow-ramping generators, which cannot adjust output quickly enough to match sudden changes in demand. This could expose generators to penalties under the Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) for deviations beyond their control.
AI data centres consume substantially more power than conventional facilities. Their demand patterns can also fluctuate sharply, depending on usage, especially LLMs, server distribution and the time zones of their customers.
The issue reached the Central Electricity Authority’s National Power Committee in February. Minutes of its meeting noted that “data centres typically exhibit high constant loads, with possible ramping characteristics depending on global time zones and server distribution”.
A committee constituted by Grid-India was tasked with studying data-centre electricity demand patterns, media reports suggest.
Alok Kumar, Director-General of the All-India Discoms Association (AIDA), told The Hindu that the incremental demand from data centres would remain manageable.
“An incremental demand from data centres ranging between one and two gigawatts per year will not make a huge difference,” he said, adding that “[moreover], this would be concentrated in certain cities only, like in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Chennai, Visakhapatnam and the Delhi NCR region, among others.”
However, the final leg of electricity transmission could pose a challenge. State transmission utilities would need to expand capacity quickly in locations witnessing a concentration of data-centre projects.
“State transmission utilities would have to quickly upgrade where there is demand and within time. It could be a challenge in certain urban areas because of right of way (RoW)-related issues,” Mr. Kumar said.
Nationwide deliberations
Concerns over data-centre loads and their implications for grid stability have surfaced across regional power committees.
At meetings of the Northern Regional Power Committee’s Operation Coordination Sub-Committee last year, officials repeatedly discussed monitoring data centres’ compliance with grid-connection requirements before supplying them with electricity.
In an email in February, the Northern Regional Load Despatch Centre, which oversees the region’s grid, warned that data centres could switch to backup power systems rapidly, creating a “credible risk of abrupt load rejection”.
Documents showed that Noida had 125 MW of operational data-centre capacity, with more than four times that capacity in the pipeline.
The Southern Regional Power Committee, meanwhile, has been preparing for a surge in demand from data-centre projects in Visakhapatnam (Google was not named in the discussions, it is the largest planned project in the area). Officials discussed the prospect of gigawatt-scale demand emerging in the region over the coming months.
At an April meeting, the SRPC’s Protection Coordination Sub-Committee examined the implications of data centres for transmission infrastructure. An official noted in the opening remarks that “inputs were sought from Grid-India to assess reserve requirements and system planning implications”.
Who pays for upgrades?
Mr. Kumar said the cost of upgrades should not become a broader financial burden, as transmission investments would ultimately be recovered through transmission charges.
However, he emphasised that data-centre operators must bear the costs of additional investments required to extend transmission infrastructure to their facilities. Such expenditure, he argued, should not be passed on to all consumers of the same distribution company.
Mr. Kumar pointed to Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) regulations that mandate this principle.
Line faults expose vulnerabilities
Maharashtra, home to a large share of India’s data centres, has long benefited from demand generated by the banking and financial services industry.
Yet the concentration of these facilities is also increasing the importance of grid reliability. Minutes of a Western Regional Power Committee meeting last year recorded discussions on a grid incident on June 12, when a faulty bus caused two interconnecting transformers to trip, resulting in the shedding of about 32 MW of data-centre load.
At a meeting in January, an official also warned that the proposed splitting (“line-in line-out”), of the Talegaon-Kharghar transmission line could leave the already stressed corridor vulnerable to severe overloading if another line tripped. The corridor serves an area experiencing growing data-centre development around Mumbai.
The official, from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited, suggested upgrading the line to 2,100 MVA.

briefs.headline: Ownership issues cloud TVS’ Venu Srinivasan, family
briefs.deck: Sudarshan Venu, the 37-year-old CMD of TVS Motor Company, named as Significant Beneficial Owner (SBO) sets cats among pigeons
briefs.bodyText:
Significant differences have emerged over the interpretation of ownership and succession plans within the family of Venu Srinivasan, involving his wife, Mallika Srinivasan, daughter Lakshmi Venu and son Sudarshan Venu, in relation to their interests in TVS Motor Company and its holding firm, TVS Holdings Limited. They are the third and fourth generation members of the TVS Group founder T.V. Sundaram Iyengar’s family.
The differences came into focus in April 2025, The Hindu has reliably learned, when TVS Holdings disclosed that Sudarshan Venu, the 37-year-old chairman and managing director of TVS Motor Company was named as a Significant Beneficial Owner (SBO). The company’s shareholding disclosure records April 16, 2025, as the date of acquisition of his significant beneficial interest through the VS Trust, in which his father, Venu Srinivasan, is a trustee, and the Srinivasan Trust.
Also read: Explainer | A look at the TVS Group’s proposed recast of holdings
The disclosure has drawn attention to the succession of ownership of TVS Motor, the flagship business within the TVS Group, valued at over ₹1.80 lakh crore.
The disagreement centres on the interpretation of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) among the four family members, dated March 20, 2024, and executed on March 21. Its salient features were disclosed to the stock exchanges on March 22. The MoU sets out non-compete obligations and restrictions on the use of the TVS brand and trademarks in specified businesses. TVS Holdings clarified that it was not a party to the agreement.
Under the disclosed terms, Mr. Sudarshan and persons controlled by him agreed not to use certain trademarks, including TVS, in specified die-casting businesses, and not to compete for a defined period in agricultural machinery, including tractors and self-propelled farm equipment. Ms. Mallika and Ms. Lakshmi, in turn, agreed not to use certain trademarks in businesses including two- and three-wheelers, financial services and real estate, and not to compete in specified vehicle-related businesses.
An executive with direct knowledge of the ongoing dispute said the MoU did not discuss ownership transition. “Does any CEO or MD automatically, become the owner as well? When we look across India, or globally, it’s stating the obvious - the distinction between distributed ownership and management,” the executive said. The executive said attempts to seek clarity on the April 2025 SBO disclosure had been met with “silence”.
Ms. Lakshmi is understood to have the support of her mother, Ms. Mallika, in seeking an amicable resolution. “She wishes to sit across and settle differences,” the executive said, adding that Ms. Lakshmi sought an equal share of the business, as the division reflected in the disclosures and the MoU was considered “very unfair”.
The dispute has also brought allegations of gender bias into focus. An executive said Ms. Mallika and Mr. Venu had raised their children to believe in equality as a value, and that the present arrangement was at odds with this principle. “What Ms. Lakshmi is asking for is equality in ownership, and Ms. Mallika supports her on this, but has emphasised on an amicable resolution,” the executive said.
Ms. Lakshmi and Ms. Mallika are also understood to be concerned about the inclusion of the Amalgamations Group in the succession discussions. “Ms. Mallika is herself only a shareholder in that group, so how can she speak for herself without even consulting other shareholding members of the family? She is running TAFE only as a custodian of the firm,” the executive said, describing the inclusion of the Amalgamations Group in the ownership tussle as “mischievous”.
The wider family arrangement provides important context. The Memorandum of Family Arrangement, dated December 10, 2020, covered four branches of the TVS family and sought to align ownership of businesses with the branches managing them and reduce cross-holdings. The arrangement was disclosed to the stock exchanges in December 2020, with further details provided in January 2021. Its implementation involved subsequent corporate restructuring, with February 4, 2022, marking an important date in the process.
The restructuring left Mr. Venu’s branch with control of the group’s flagship automotive interests through TVS Holdings, which was formed out of the restructuring of the erstwhile Sundaram-Clayton. TVS Holdings now holds 50.26% of TVS Motor Company. The separate Sundaram-Clayton entity houses the die-casting business. The ownership structure of these entities is central to the dispute as the family settlement aligned the ownership of businesses with the branches managing them.
The settlement also involved obligations of about ₹2,000 crore payable to other family branches. According to TVS Holdings’ information memorandum, Sundaram-Clayton diluted about 7% of its stake in TVS Motor in FY2022, raising about ₹2,100 crore. The company’s disclosures also describe financing arrangements connected with the settlement obligations. Subsequent reports have attributed the funding and settlement of the dues to Mr. Venu Srinivasan and Mr. Sudarshan Venu.
Lawyers who spoke to The Hindu said an SBO declaration, by itself, should not be construed as a transfer of ownership. Corporate lawyer Karthik Sheshadri, who practises before the Madras High Court, said the primary document underlying the declaration must be examined. “A primary document can be a trust deed, an arrangement, a transfer document, that may not necessarily be disclosed as that is not a requirement, but it has to be the basis for a SBO disclosure,” he said.
“Regulatory filings can be unilateral, which is why it has irked one party. And often, such filings are done at a corporate secretarial level, and they would do it on behalf of the person who controls the company. This is where disputes arise,” Mr. Sheshadri added.

briefs.headline: Despite promise, builder denied disabled parking to Rs 1.03 crore flat buyer; RERA orders relief
briefs.deck: In one such case, a woman and her family bought a 3BHK ( 3 Bedrooms, Hall, Kitchen) from a builder in Bengaluru for Rs 1.03 crore. The builder promised two specially enabled parking spaces, and it was supposedly one of the property's key attractions. The builder's brochure and terms clearly referred to these parking facilities. However, he failed to deliver on that commitment.
briefs.bodyText:
You buy an apartment with the builder promising some special parking provisions. But the builder fails to deliver and collects steep maintenance charges from residents. What do you do?
In one such case, a woman and her family bought a 3BHK ( 3 Bedrooms, Hall, Kitchen) from a builder in Bengaluru for Rs 1.03 crore. The builder promised two specially enabled parking spaces, and it was supposedly one of the property's key attractions.
What the case is about
The builder's brochure and terms clearly referred to these parking facilities. However, he failed to deliver on that commitment.
However, the problems did not end there. Although the family executed the sale deed in August 2024, the builder has still not formed an apartment association.
Also Read | 
Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing parties
Not only that, he has allegedly been collecting steep maintenance charges from residents without offering a proper explanation or producing audited accounts to justify the amounts.
Frustrated by the builder's conduct, the woman approached the Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) to seek legal action.
On September 7, 2026, the Karnataka RERA tribunal ruled in her favour and also strongly criticised the builder for undermining homebuyers' expectations.
Also Read | 
She worked as a teacher till 62 years of age instead of retiring at 60, but was denied gratuity because of extended service; Allahabad HC orders payment with 6% interest
Why did the homebuyer win the case?
Subrata Mukherjee, Partner at SNG & Partners, Advocates & Solicitors, told ET that the homebuyer succeeded because Karnataka-RERA concluded that the builder was obligated to provide a separate car parking space for a physically challenged person.
This took into account the specific regulatory requirements governing the project and the evidence submitted before the Authority.
The homebuyers purchased the apartment under a Sale Deed dated August 6, 2024, for a total consideration of Rs 1,03,28,979.
In December 2023, the builder sent an email to the homebuyer, assuring her that a specially enabled parking space would be provided. However, the promised facility was not made available.
The woman then wrote to the builder, reminding about the applicable guidelines requiring the provision of specially enabled parking.
She relied on the environmental clearance issued by the Karnataka government. Clause 32 of the clearance specifies that facilities such as ramps and separate parking spaces must be provided for physically challenged persons.
Considering these exchanges alongside the specific conditions in the project's Environmental Clearance, the Authority concluded that the builder was obligated to provide the required facility.
After examining this provision, the Karnataka RERA tribunal observed that the guidelines clearly required the builder to make arrangements for facilities, including ramps and dedicated parking spaces, for persons with disabilities.
RERA said: “Hence, viewed from any angle, the respondent (builder) is bound to provide separate car parking for physically challenged.”
On this basis, the tribunal directed the builder to provide parking spaces for specially enabled persons in the housing project within 60 days from the date of the order.
Karnataka-RERA also held that the builder was required to establish an association of allottees in accordance with the applicable law once the project had been completed in all respects and the occupancy certificate or completion certificate had been obtained.
Following the formation of the association, the builder would have to execute the deed of declaration and provide audited accounts along with details of the maintenance charges.
Accordingly, the tribunal directed the builder to furnish audited accounts and revised maintenance charges while executing the Deed of Declaration. This was to be done after the project was fully completed, the Occupancy Certificate or Completion Certificate was obtained, and an Association of Allottees was formed in accordance with the law in force.

briefs.headline: Man faces Rs 17.18 lakh tax penalty over Rs 55.62 lakh unexplained deposits; ITAT gives relief
briefs.deck: A man had not filed an income tax return for assessment year 2016-17. The tax department subsequently completed a reassessment without his participation and, on February 15, 2024, assessed his total income at Rs 55.62 lakh. The amount was treated as unexplained cash deposits in a bank account that the department attributed to him.
briefs.bodyText:
Unexplained cash can lead to a notice from the Income Tax Department, and sometimes even a penalty. But what happens if the penalty is imposed under the wrong section?
In one such case, the Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled that a tax officer cannot impose a penalty under one provision of the Income Tax Act when the assessment order records that proceedings were being initiated under different provisions.
What the case is about
A man had not filed an income tax return for assessment year 2016-17. The tax department subsequently completed a reassessment without his participation and, on February 15, 2024, assessed his total income at Rs 55.62 lakh.
The amount was treated as unexplained cash deposits in a bank account that the department attributed to him. The assessment order referred to Section 68 at one point and later treated the amount as unexplained money under Section 69. It also directed that tax be charged under Section 115BBE.
Also Read | 
Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemption
At the end of the assessment order, the officer recorded that penalty proceedings were being initiated under Sections 271AAC and 272A(1)(d).
The tax department also imposed a penalty, but under Section 271(1)(c), which deals with concealment of income or furnishing inaccurate particulars of income. On August 21, 2024, the officer levied a penalty of Rs 17,18,658, calculated at 100% of the tax sought to be evaded.
The man challenged the penalty, but the National Faceless Appeal Centre, Delhi, upheld it on January 23, 2026. He then approached the tribunal.
Why he won relief from penalty in ITAT
His objections went beyond the penalty. He argued that he was a non-resident and that the bank account did not belong to him. He also pointed out references in the assessment order to assessment year 2019-20 and financial year 2018-19, rather than the year under consideration.
Those issues concern the underlying tax assessment, which the man has challenged separately. The tribunal did not decide them in this appeal. It focused on whether the officer could legally impose a penalty under Section 271(1)(c) when the assessment order had recorded the initiation of proceedings under other provisions.
Also Read | 
Man opted for VRS after employer shut plant, got Rs 65.21 lakh and reported it as advance salary in ITR; Section 89 relief was denied, but ITAT Pune later ruled it a non-taxable capital receipt
The tribunal went back to the assessment order to establish exactly what the officer had recorded. Its finding was straightforward: the order mentioned Sections 271AAC and 272A(1)(d), but contained no corresponding direction to initiate penalty proceedings under Section 271(1)(c).
That omission was central to the case. Section 271(1B) provides for deemed satisfaction in specified circumstances where an assessment order contains a direction to initiate penalty proceedings under Section 271(1)(c). The tribunal found that the necessary direction was missing here.
The officer could not simply switch to a different penalty provision later, the tribunal held. Sections 271AAC and 271(1)(c) are distinct provisions, and initiating proceedings under one does not amount to initiating them under the other.
There was also a problem with the penalty order itself. It stated that proceedings under Section 271(1)(c) had been initiated during the assessment. But the assessment order did not support that statement. The tribunal held that the later order could not make good the missing requirement or change what had been recorded earlier.
Amit Gupta, Partner at Saraf and Partners says that the judgement emphasizes on the rule of the law with respect to distinction between penalty proceedings, vis-à-vis, underlying assessment proceedings.
“It’s important to note that proceedings for imposition of penalty even though the same may emanate from assessment, are independent,” he tells TOI.
According to Gupta, the judgement goes to highlight that the taxpayer can very well challenge the vires of the penalty proceedings independently and the merits/validity of the assessment or reassessment in pursuance of which penalty is levied can be challenged separately but cannot be the subject matter of penalty proceedings.
Also Read | 
Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claim
Chapter XXI in the Income tax Act, 1961 enacts provisions for the levy, imposition and collection of penalty. It plays an integral role for the effective implementation of the tax statute and acts as an important deterrent for the evasion of tax by taxpayers.
Section 271(1) makes appropriate provision to regulate levy of penalties on assessee in case of concealment of income or furnishing of inaccurate particulars of such income.
“Accordingly, the existence of conditions stipulated in Section 271(1)(c) are a sine qua non for initiation of penalty proceedings under Section 271 and such existence should be clearly reflected in the underlying assessment order,” Gupta explains.
“Furthermore, power to impose a penalty under section 271(1) hinges upon the satisfaction of the concerned officer in the course of assessment proceedings and it cannot be exercised if he is not satisfied and has not recorded his satisfaction about the existence of conditions,” he adds.
Equally essential is the direction to initiate proceedings under Section 271(l)(c) which is pre-requisite for initiation of the penalty proceedings because of the deeming provision contained in Section 271(1B) of the ITA.
In this backdrop, ITAT held the penalty initiation under Section 271(1)(c ) was without jurisdiction since the Assessing Officer had specifically initiated penalty proceedings under Section 271AAC (applicable to certain unexplained income taxable under Section 115BBE) and not under Section 271(1)(c) relating to concealment of income or furnishing inaccurate particulars.
Also Read | 
Man paid Rs 1.73 crore for Gurgaon flat, waited over a decade without possession; builder alleges homebuyer bought it for commercial gain, consumer commission awards refund with 12% interest & Rs 4 lakh
“Since the assessment order contained no satisfaction or direction for initiation of penalty under Section 271(1)(c), the subsequent levy under that provision was held to be invalid and an incurable jurisdictional defect since penalty provisions are distinct and cannot be interchanged. Initiation under Section 271AAC cannot be treated as initiation under Section 271(1)(c),” Gupta says.
The tribunal explained that the validity of the penalty was a separate question from whether the Rs 55.62 lakh addition would ultimately stand. Even if the addition were upheld, the penalty could not survive without valid initiation under Section 271(1)(c).
Nor did the tribunal see a reason to wait for the pending appeal over the addition. The tribunal therefore deleted the penalty of Rs 17,18,658.
It’s important to note that the decision is limited to that penalty. It does not establish that the cash deposits were wrongly treated as income, or that the disputed bank account did not belong to the man.

briefs.headline: U.S.-Ukraine-European negotiators meet in Miami as Trump announces diesel deal with Russia
briefs.deck: The goal is to reach agreement on such a proposal in the coming weeks so it can be presented ‌to Russia in order to seek a breakthrough before the winter
briefs.bodyText:
Negotiators for the U.S., Ukraine and Europeans held six hours of talks in Miami on Friday (October 9, 2026) with the aim of reaching agreement on a unified proposal to end the war in Ukraine, a person familiar with the talks said.
The goal is to reach agreement on such a proposal in the coming weeks so it can be presented to Russia in order to seek a breakthrough before the winter, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
The talks came on the same day that U.S. President Donald Trump said Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices, while his administration lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for the war. The deal was criticised by U.S. lawmakers and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
"All that money goes toward the war against people, against Ukraine, against all of us. I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair," Mr. Zelenskyy said in a statement.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said after a call with Mr. Trump that an immediate resumption of peace talks was unlikely, citing Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow.
The talks in Miami included U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and delegations from Ukraine as well as representatives from Europe and NATO.
The negotiators covered a lengthy list of topics in the discussions, including a post-war package for Ukraine that would include security guarantees from the U.S. and from Europe, the person said.
Also discussed were a post-war economic plan for Ukraine and a pathway to accession to the European Union for Kyiv, the person said.
In a sensitive subject, the delegations discussed "some ideas" on territory, the person said, declining to elaborate.
Ukraine has been adamant that Russia cede territory it has seized during the conflict. President Donald Trump has said both sides will need to compromise.
The person said the delegations also discussed a Europe-Russia security architecture that would set the stage for peaceful years ahead. The person did not provide details.

stories.headline: Real Madrid's Viní Jr issues apology after red card: What happens next
stories.deck: Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior apologised to teammates and fans after being sent off for pulling Villarreal defender Nathan Saliba’s hair during Saturday’s 1-0 win. He could miss the October 25 El Clásico against Barcelona, depending on his suspension. Meanwhile, Barcelona beat Getafe 3-0, extending their perfect LaLiga start to eight wins and strengthening their lead at the top.
stories.bodyText:
Real Madrid forward Vinícius Júnior has apologised to his teammates and fans after receiving a straight red card during their 1-0 LaLiga victory over Villarreal at the Santiago Bernabéu on Saturday.
The Brazilian now faces the possibility of missing the crucial El Clásico against Barcelona on October 25, depending on the disciplinary committee’s decision.
Vinícius came on as a second-half substitute and was sent off around 20 minutes later after a VAR review showed him pulling Villarreal defender Nathan Saliba’s hair.
His apparent second goal was ruled out, leaving Real Madrid to defend their narrow lead with 10 players.
After the match, the 26-year-old took to social media to apologise, writing, "sorry to the team and the fans."
Possible suspension for El Clásico
Spanish Football Federation rules classify hair-pulling as violent conduct. Under Article 130, such an offence can result in a suspension of one to three matches if no injury is caused.
Real Madrid’s next three league fixtures are against Sevilla, Barcelona and Racing Santander. A ban covering the October 25 clash at Camp Nou would be a major setback for the Spanish giants, with Vinícius awaiting the final decision.
Barcelona maintain perfect start
Meanwhile, Barcelona continued their impressive start to the LaLiga season with a comfortable 3-0 home win over Getafe, securing their eighth consecutive victory.
Anthony Gordon opened the scoring inside two minutes with a deflected effort, while Gabriel Jesus doubled the advantage in the 30th minute on his first start for the club.
Jules Koundé sealed the win in the 73rd minute, heading home a cross from Lamine Yamal. Barcelona remain top of the standings with 24 points.

stories.headline: 'Stupid boy': England cricket legend Botham reignites feud with Stokes
stories.deck: England legend Ian Botham has reignited his feud with Ben Stokes, calling him a "stupid boy" and a "has-been" over England’s Ashes preparations and retirement. Botham criticised the team’s lack of practice matches and trip to Noosa after defeats. Stokes defended modern cricket’s demands and hit back online, saying, "it's better to be a has-been than a never-been."
stories.bodyText:
England cricket great Ian Botham has reignited his public feud with former England captain Ben Stokes, calling him a "stupid boy" and a "has-been" after their disagreement over England’s Ashes preparations and Stokes’ retirement.
Botham and Stokes, both regarded as among England’s finest all-rounders, have exchanged criticism over the past year. The dispute began when Botham questioned England’s preparations for the Ashes in Australia, arguing that the team should have played at least one state match before the series.
Speaking to The Times Magazine, Botham criticised Stokes over the team’s approach and their decision to visit Noosa after losing the first two matches of the Ashes series. He said, "Stupid boy. I'll mention him only briefly because his self-indulgence is not something I enjoy."
Although Botham praised Stokes as a great player, he questioned the team’s choices during the tour. Referring to their time in Noosa, he added, "Really? They were p****d as rats. Look, if you want a drink, don't go to the high street. We used to go to wineries."
Botham had earlier said England’s failure to arrange a state match was a sign of arrogance, adding, "Not one (state match), which borders on arrogance. 
You've got to give yourself the chance."
Stokes defended the team’s approach, pointing to changes in the modern game. He said, "There's quite a few factors that play into why we can't prepare how the has-beens maybe prepared in the past. The landscape of cricket has changed and that affects preparation."
Stokes fires back
After Stokes retired from England duty earlier this year, Botham mocked him during an appearance on 
Test Match Special
. He said, "As we know Michael Vaughan and I, we don't know what we're talking about. Couple of old has-beens."
Addressing Stokes directly, he added, "Ben, if you're listening, congratulations, you've joined the club - you're now a has-been."
Stokes responded on X with a pointed remark, "The quote 'it's better to be a has-been than a never-been' originates from Lord Ian Botham."
Botham has now taken another swipe at Stokes while releasing his new book, saying, "This is for you, Ben. Welcome to the has-beens club." The exchange shows that the disagreement between the two former England stars remains unresolved.

stories.headline: Flamboyant Badoni keen to put a price on his wicket
stories.deck: While the middle-order batter’s average of 54 in the longer format is noteworthy, his return of four hundreds and 10 half-centuries after 38 innings suggests the need to be more ruthless in his pursuit of runs
stories.bodyText:
On the eve of a new Ranji Trophy season, Delhi’s Ayush Badoni faces a daunting test. The 26-year-old will be expected to not just score a heap of runs in the middle-order and guide Delhi’s young batting unit, but also hit the right notes as captain and resurrect his team’s fortunes in the First Class competition. The seven-time Ranji champion hasn’t entered the knockouts since 2017-18.
It isn’t in Badoni’s nature to shy away from a challenge. “I like to take challenges. As a batter, I like it when there is pressure. As a captain too, there is pressure. I will try to keep things simple and rely on my instincts to do what is best in that given moment,” he told The Hindu on Saturday ahead of Delhi’s opening fixture against Bengal in Kalyani.
While Badoni’s average of 54 in the longer format is noteworthy, his return of four hundreds and 10 half-centuries after 38 innings suggests the need to be more ruthless in his pursuit of runs.
“I want to put a price on my wicket. There have been instances when I have played some flamboyant shots to give away my wicket. I want to make the bowlers earn my wicket. If I make a half-century, I don’t want to get carried away. I want to get as many big scores as possible,” he said.
In recent Ranji campaigns, Delhi’s inability to consistently pick 20 wickets has contributed severely to its travails. In the joust against Bengal, the onus will be on pacers Navdeep Saini, Simarjeet Singh, Money Grewal and Divij Mehra to show the way.
“Injuries have been common. We have not always had our main bowlers available,” the skipper lamented. “Apart from Saini, there isn’t much experience. It does take some time. But the hope is that the bowlers have evolved and will take a lot of wickets this season.”

stories.headline: The Gymkhana gets a makeover
stories.bodyText:
Before Hyderabad had a Test venue, it had Gymkhana.
Cricket has been played on this ground for more than 150 years, ever since British army personnel first took to it in the 19th century. In 1931 it staged its first First Class match and three years later the MCC became the first official overseas team to play in Hyderabad, and this was the ground that welcomed them.
The Women’s World Cup, the Irani Cup and many others have come to this patch of Secunderabad.
With the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium due for much-needed revamp, Gymkhana will host all of Hyderabad’s matches in the Ranji Trophy’s 2026-27 season – and set the ball rolling there.
“Gymkhana has produced a lot of cricketers for India and is the birthplace of cricket in Hyderabad. After taking charge, I went and saw Gymkhana, and it was not the same ground that I knew,” HCA secretary M. Jeevan Reddy told The Hindu.
Soon after Ambati Rayudu became HCA’s head of cricket operations, he vowed to even out gains for batters and bowlers from surfaces here and gear pitches towards producing results.
Roughly four months of labour and close to one crore in expenditure later, all nine pitches – four of black soil, three of red, and two with a 50-50 mix (all sourced from Vikarabad) – at Gymkhana wear a fresh face, done under the watchful eyes of D. Mukesh Kumar, HCA’s senior curator.
Hyderabad and Tripura will be the first to find out what they offer, but the early impressions have already won over head coaches Anirudh Singh and Satrajit Lahiri respectively.
The 30-yard circle has also been rebuilt from the ground up so that the surface is no longer as unforgiving on players’ bodies. The drainage system has also been reworked, which has in turn helped the square boundary grow by around six yards.

briefs.headline: Harmanpreet Kaur | The game changer
briefs.deck: The cricketer who helped popularise women’s cricket in India has stepped down as captain but will continue to play for the national team
briefs.bodyText:
Dressed in a dark blue blazer and white trousers, her hair gathered in a tight ponytail and her hands clasped behind her back, Harmanpreet Kaur is looking at the famous balcony at Lord’s. The camera has captured the moment from behind, as she stands there at cricket’s best-known venue, situated in northwest London.
The picture seems to have been taken in July, during the photoshoot ahead of the historic Women’s Test match between India and England. It was the first-ever women’s Test at Lord’s, the history of which dates back 239 years. Harmanpreet chose that image for the Instagram post through which she announced her decision to step down as the India captain. Harmanpreet’s fairly long and well-written message was posted on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) . It has had 1.4 million views and about 30,500 comments.
Not everyone who viewed the photograph in the post would have been a long-time follower of women’s cricket. It is not even a decade since female practitioners of India’s favourite obsession began to be known beyond their families and friends, apart from a small circle of committed supporters.
And it was Harmanpreet who forced the Indian cricket fan to take a closer look at the women’s game. In the semifinal of the 2017 World Cup at Derby, she played an innings that still remains perhaps the greatest played by a woman. Her 171 not out off just 115 balls stunned defending champions Australia. Former Australian captain Alyssa Healy said it even forced her team to change the way it played its cricket.
Innings of a lifetime
Harmanpreet’s own hero, Virender Sehwag, called it an innings of a lifetime and tweeted, “Harmanpreet Kaur...Fan!” When she was a little girl growing up in Punjab’s Moga, wanting to be a cricketer, when hardly anyone there knew women even played the game, she used to be teased by her brother, “What will you do — open with Sehwag?”
Two years after that out-of-the-world knock, Harmanpreet had told this writer, during an interview in Surat, how much she used to wish for people to come and watch women play cricket. She was grateful destiny chose her to play a part in making it possible.
Harmanpreet was the catalyst, but it was the BCCI’s decision to take women’s cricket under its wings that brought visibility and professionalism to the game. Then the launch of the Women’s Premier League (WPL), in 2023, and India’s victory at the ODI World Cup at home last year have expanded the fan base. Harmanpreet was the captain who led India to that World Cup win; it was India’s first global trophy in women’s cricket. She was also the skipper when the Mumbai Indians emerged as the WPL champion in the inaugural edition.
She has had a lot of success in recent times, too. Under her captaincy, India won the Asia Cup and then the gold medal at the Asian Games. Before that, India crushed England in that Test match at Lord’s. That was only her fifth Test as captain. That women get to play very few matches in the game’s finest format remains a cause for concern even in these rosy times. She led India in 51 One-Day Internationals and 155 Twenty20 Internationals.
Overall, she has played eight Tests, 164 ODIs and 210 T20Is. Those numbers could grow further, as she has clearly said she wants to continue to play for India, though she has resigned as captain. She has plenty to offer as a player, and India needs her in the line-up. She remains one of the best batters in the game. Few women could hit a cricket ball as hard as she could. Her ability to hit hard was noticed early. And she had worked hard on that. Her first coach Yadwinder Singh made her hit 100 to 150 sixes every day. She debuted for India in 2009. Three years later, she led the country for the first time at the Asia Cup in 2012 — it would take a few years before she was made captain full-time — and India emerged as champions. She went on to lead India in many more memorable wins.
As she looked at the Lord’s balcony that sunny day in July, in the twilight of her career, some of those images may have passed through her mind.

briefs.headline: Coach Asnodkar wants Kerala to do well in all the formats
briefs.bodyText:
Eighteen years later, Swapnil Asnodkar still remembers that loose shot he played against Sreekumar Nair at Palakkad. It is, after all, not every day that you get a chance to score a double-hundred.
After opening the innings for Goa, he was dismissed for 191 against Kerala in that Ranji Trophy match in the 2008-09 season. He was the Goa captain then and enjoyed his team’s battles with Kerala. Now he is glad that he is coaching Kerala.
“I am looking forward to this game and the wicket looks good,” Asnodkar told The Hindu on the eve of Kerala’s first Ranji match of the season, against Jharkhand, starting here on Sunday. “We are ready for it. It is up to the boys now to go and express themselves.”
Having worked with the Kerala Under-23 side, Asnodkar was only happy to take up the offer to coach the senior team. The goal he has set for the team is not just for the Ranji Trophy. “We need to do well in all the formats,” he said. “And we are not thinking about things like qualifying for the knock-out at the moment.”
Asnodkar is glad that Jalaj Saxena and Aditya Sarwate are back in the Kerala team. “Their return takes care of our spin attack,” he said. “It is good to have such experience in the team.”
He is also banking on the experience of Sachin Baby, the key man in batting. “He has been playing for the last 17 years,” he said. “And he is looking hungry.”

briefs.headline: Marathas blank Chiefs; Yodhas win a thriller
briefs.bodyText:
Mighty Marathas registered the first clean sweep of Archery Premier League season-2, beating Chola Chiefs 6-0 at People’s Plaza here on Saturday.
Led by Mike Schloesser and anchored by Dhiraj Bommadevara under time pressure, Marathas brought up their first win of the campaign in style. Schloesser lived up to his ‘Mr. Perfect’ nickname, shooting 10s with all six arrows for Marathas.
Chiefs stuck to their tactic of having their compound archers shoot back-to-back at the start of the set, but Chikitha Taniparthi’s two 9s put a dent in their plans and they fell behind. After that, Marathas did enough to comfortably stay ahead and seal the win.
Chero Archers and Prithviraj Yodhas then played out the most nail-biting contest of the evening, with both going toe-to-toe to take the match into a hit-or-miss. There was little to separate the two there too, much to the delight of the packed stands.
Matias Grande finally managed to find the inner ring, sending the Yodhas’ camp into loud celebrations. Pritika Pradeep couldn’t emulate Grade, giving Yodhas a thrilling victory.
In the final match, Kakatiya Knights came from behind to emerge victorious against Rajputana Royals.
Neeraj shines
Neeraj Chauhan was the star for Knights, coming up with clutch X-ring 10s while Jyothi Surekha Vennam was also on fire.
While Mete Gazoz helped Royals take the first set with a pressure 10 in the first set, it was Neeraj and Jyothi who led Knights’ fightback. They, in fact, missed the perfect 80 after Neeraj could only come up with a nine with the final arrow of the day.

briefs.headline: Kerala eyes good start against a strong Jharkhand side
briefs.bodyText:
The Keenan Stadium is named after John Keenan, an American. He was a much-loved general manager who played a key role in the growth of Tata Steel.
A cricket ground honouring an American isn’t usual. But, that isn’t the only claim to fame for this ground.
It was here that Viv Richards smashed a 99-ball 149 in an ODI for the West Indies against India in 1983, which was basically a revenge tour for Clive Lloyd’s men for their World Cup loss to Kapil Dev’s Devils.
Sourav Ganguly scored a hundred in an Indian victory in 2000 against South Africa, while M.S. Dhoni fell four runs short of one against England six years later.
Those glory days are behind this ground.
But it remains a prominent venue for Ranji Trophy. And Kerala begins its campaign in the new season, with a match against Jharkhand, here on Sunday.
Vishnu Vinod’s men should be looking for a fine start, especially after the disappointment of the last season.
For a team that created history in 2024-25, by reaching the final, the last edition of India’s premier domestic tourney didn’t go well at all. Kerala finished fifth in a group of eight.
This time around, Kerala is grouped with the likes of Delhi, Bengal, Maharashtra and Gujarat. And Jharkhand had played the quarterfinals last season, after topping its pool.
The return of Jalaj Saxena and Aditya Sarwate has sharpened the attack. When it comes to batting, Sachin Baby’s experience and calmness continues to be reassuring, but the likes of Rohan Kunnummal, Vishnu, Salman Nizar and Mohammed Azharuddeen have to be more consistent.
The host’s batting boasts players like Shikhar Mohan, Sharandeep Singh and captain Virat Singh, but it will miss the services of Kumar Kushagra, who is playing for India-A against Australia-A.

briefs.headline: Arsenal survive Leeds scare as Arteta’s inspired triple substitution sparks comeback win
briefs.deck: Arsenal secured a crucial 2-1 comeback victory against Leeds United at the Emirates Stadium. The match saw Leeds initially take the lead in the second half through James Justin's goal after a counterattack. However, Riccardo Calafiori equalised shortly after, before Bruno Guimaraes scored the winner. Mikel Arteta acknowledged the importance of the win following a prior loss to Brighton & Hove…
briefs.bodyText:
Mikel Arteta
’s Arsenal survived a major scare against a feisty Leeds United to return to winning ways in the Premier League, recovering from a second-half deficit to claim a 2-1 victory at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday.
After struggling to break down Leeds’ well-organised defence for much of the first half, Arsenal fell behind in the 55th minute when James Justin blasted home after Gabriel Gudmundsson’s delivery found its way across the penalty area.
But Riccardo Calafiori restored parity seven minutes later before substitute Bruno Guimaraes completed the comeback in the 70th minute, sparing Arsenal the prospect of a second successive league defeat.
The victory was a timely response after Arsenal’s disappointing 0-3 loss to Brighton & Hove Albion in their last outing before the international break. It also provided a perfect celebration after Arteta signed a contract extension earlier in the week.
Leeds test Arsenal’s patience
Leeds frustrated the hosts with disciplined defending and threatened on the counterattack, making life difficult for an Arsenal side that struggled to turn promising attacking positions into clear-cut opportunities.
“They are extremely well-organised, they are very physical, they are committed in everything that they do,” Arteta told TNT Sports.
The Arsenal manager admitted his side had failed to make the most of their attacking opportunities in the first half, while conceding too many free kicks, throw-ins and set pieces.
“When you don't finish the actions, and we hit some great areas in the first half to have much more end product than we did, and we lost the ball just before the last action, and when that happens and they had moments to run, they are a threat,” he explained.
Calafiori’s equaliser, which came after Ben White headed the ball back across goal, shifted the momentum. It was the Italian defender’s sixth goal for Arsenal, but his first at the Emirates.
Arteta’s triple change turns the tide
Arteta’s decision to introduce Guimaraes, Viktor Gyokeres and Jurrien Timber in the 63rd minute proved decisive, adding fresh energy, physicality and attacking intent.
The winner arrived seven minutes later after a quickly taken free kick led to a slick passing move, with Declan Rice setting up Guimaraes to drive the ball into the bottom-left corner from outside the area.
“We bring a lot of leadership in those three players — we brought a goal threat, we brought people who can win duels because it was very man-orientated, people that can get away from that, people that can play forward and penetrate,” Arteta said.
The result moved Arsenal level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table, ahead of City’s match against Liverpool on Sunday.
After weeks without his full squad during the international break, Arteta was relieved to see his players respond.
“We reacted incredibly well. We really need to enjoy the victory, because we are realising how this Premier League is going to pan out,” he said.

briefs.headline: National Open Athletics: Anushka Yadav claims hammer throw gold
briefs.bodyText:
National record-holder Anushka Yadav added the National champion tag to her name to round up an eventful year, claiming the hammer throw gold on day three of the National open athletics championships here on Saturday.
The 18-year-old Anushka, among the few Asian Games participants to enter this competition, threw to a distance of 66.53m to better the previous meet record of Manju Rani by more than two metres. Interestingly, Anushka, who finished fifth at Aichi-Nagoya, also managed a better throw than her performance there — her Saturday’s mark could have helped her finish one position higher and ahead of teammate and former NR holder Tanya Chaudhary.
Also doing better than what he could manage at the Asian Games was shot-putter Karanveer Singh, taking the top spot with a best throw of 19.63m. Karanveer had finished a disappointing 10th and his performance at the Jawharlal Nehru Stadium, more than a metre more than the 18.40m at the Asiad, would have easily propelled him into the top-four. Railways’ Sanyam took second spot with 18.32m, same as teammate Anurag Kaler but edging ahead by virtue of having the better second-best throw of 18.25m while Anurag’s was 18.10m.
Kiran Pahal, member of the Indian quartet that won the lone athletics gold at the Asian Games, anchored the Railways side here to a comfortable gold in the 4x400m mixed relay in 3:21.60. Kiran, who was the fastest in the individual 400m heats before pulling out of the semifinals, never ceded control once Vikrant Panchal leapfrogged from third to first on the third lap before handing over the baton.

briefs.headline: Ranji Trophy: Karnataka faces Andhra test in opening match
briefs.deck: Smaran, on captaincy debut, and Vinay Kumar, for whom it will be a maiden coaching stint in charge of Karnataka, have their task cut out
briefs.bodyText:
Seven months after finishing second best to Jammu & Kashmir in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy, Karnataka will begin yet another campaign with the singular aim of bringing home the trophy that has eluded it since 2014-15.
The first outing will be against Andhra at Mulapadu near here on Sunday. But, R. Smaran, on captaincy debut (in place of Devdutt Padikkal), and R. Vinay Kumar, for whom it will be a maiden coaching stint in charge of Karnataka, have their task cut out.
While K.L. Rahul, Mayank Agarwal, Karun Nair and the in-form Smaran dominate the batting line-up, the fast-bowling department appears airy, with Prasidh Krishna, Vidwath Kaverappa, V. Vyshak and Vidyadhar Patil all out injured.
The responsibility will have to be shouldered by Abhilash Shetty and M. Venkatesh, who both have five caps each, and L. Manvanth Kumar and L.R. Kumar, both of whom are yet to make their First Class debuts.
Vinay, though, was upbeat. “We will miss some experience and quality, but I am confident in the upcoming bowlers’ ability,” he told The Hindu.
In Andhra, Karnataka has a strong opponent. Led by the seasoned Ricky Bhui and coached by the astute Kiwi Gary Stead, it has in its ranks the promising 22-year-old batter Shaik Rasheed. Off-spinner T. Vijay, who has totalled 50 First Class wickets over the past two seasons, will be keenly watched.
Four knockout appearances in the last six editions indicate quality. But it is also a fact that Andhra hasn’t gone past the quarterfinals in any of them.
“We can’t take anyone lightly; the best example is J&K, who beat us to win the title,” Vinay insisted. “Andhra is a good side, but I have always believed that if we can play at 80 to 85% of our potential, we will be very tough to beat.”
A tone-setting performance will bode well.

briefs.headline: Rajya Sabha member highlights role of chess in improving concentration, decision-making
briefs.deck: Inaugurating a chess club at Chalapathi University, Bhashyam Rama Krishna says it could serve as a model for other institutions; an All India Open Rapid Chess Tournament attracting 242 players conducted as part of the event
briefs.bodyText:
The Chalapathi University has launched a chess club to promote strategic thinking and intellectual development among students. Rajya Sabha member Bhashyam Rama Krishna and Grandmaster Koneru Humpy inaugurated the club on the university campus in Guntur on Saturday.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Rama Krishna described it as the institution’s first chess club and said it could serve as a model for other institutions. He emphasised that chess improved concentration, analytical thinking and decision-making abilities.
Pro-Chancellor Y. Sujith Kumar said the university had incorporated chess into its curriculum and provided dedicated practice slots for students. Chancellor Y.V. Anjaneyulu said equal importance was given to academics and sports, while Ms. Humpy assured support for developing chess activities. Vice-Chancellor B.V. Chowdary highlighted the game’s role in cultivating patience, focus and strategic thinking.
As part of the event an All India Open Rapid Chess Tournament was organised, which attracted 242 players from across the country, including around 96 international-level players.
Dhruvesh Dondapati emerged champion, followed by Perecherla Hariram Sai Krishna in second place and Siva Pawan Teja U. in third. K. Raju and R. Aditya secured the fourth and fifth places respectively.
The guests distributed cash prizes totalling ₹1,11,999 and certificates to the winners and runners-up and congratulated them. They also wished them success in the upcoming national and international competitions.
